proposals.before: Thereupon Dou Yan, acting head of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized that His Majesty's great-great-grandfather, Lord Wen'an of Wen Prefecture, should be titled Emperor Wenxian, temple name Xizu;
proposals.after: Thereupon Dou Yan, acting head of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized that His Majesty's great-great-grandfather, Lord Wen'an, should be titled Emperor Wenxian, temple name Xizu;
proposals.reason: 府君 is the honorific for a deceased official, not a prefecture; 文安府君 is Lord Wen'an, not Lord Wen'an of Wen Prefecture.

proposals.before: We humbly request posthumous elevation of four generations—great-great-grandfather and above—and the exalted construction of temple chambers."
proposals.after: We humbly request posthumous elevation of the four generations from the great-great-grandfather and the great-grandfather downward, and the exalted construction of temple chambers."
proposals.reason: 高、曾四代 means four ancestral generations beginning from the great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather, not merely 'great-great-grandfather and above.'

proposals.before: Tang's Zhongzong and Ruizong both occupied zhao positions, while Gaozu, Wen, and Wu shared zhao and mu as one generation.
proposals.after: Tang's Zhongzong and Ruizong both occupied zhao positions, while Jing, Wen, and Wu shared zhao and mu as one generation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 敬、文、武 are Tang Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong, the brother-generation emperors; 敬 is not 高祖/Gaozu.

proposals.before: Hanlin Academician Song Wo objected: "Since the Three Dynasties, brotherly succession has been common, but zhao and mu in different positions—this we have never seen.
proposals.after: Hanlin Academician Song Shi objected: "Since the Three Dynasties, brotherly succession has been common, but zhao and mu in different positions—this we have never seen.
proposals.reason: The official is 宋湜 (Song Shi); Wo does not match 湜.

proposals.before: Hanlin Academician Song Wo stated: "From the Three Dynasties downward, brotherly succession has been common, but zhao and mu in different positions—this we have never seen.
proposals.after: Hanlin Academician Song Shi stated: "From the Three Dynasties downward, brotherly succession has been common, but zhao and mu in different positions—this we have never seen.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise misreads 宋湜 as Song Wo.

proposals.before: Wen Jiao, on brotherly succession and storing tablets in flanking chambers, argued: 'If each emperor counts as one generation, one could not sacrifice to one's father—falling short even of a commoner's rites.'"
proposals.after: Wen Qiao, on brotherly succession and storing tablets in flanking chambers, argued: 'If each emperor counts as one generation, one could not sacrifice to one's father—falling short even of a commoner's rites.'"
proposals.reason: 溫嶠 is Wen Qiao (Qiáo); later units already use Qiao, so Jiao is an inconsistent romanization of the same man.

proposals.before: By ancient rule, the spirits of Xi and Shun should be moved.
proposals.after: By ancient rule, the spirits of Xizu and Shunzu should be moved.
proposals.reason: 僖、順 abbreviate the Song temple names 僖祖 and 順祖, not Emperor Shun; Xi/Shun as personal names misidentify the ancestral spirits.

proposals.before: According to antiquity, the spirits of Xi and Shun should be moved.
proposals.after: According to antiquity, the spirits of Xizu and Shunzu should be moved.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 僖、順 as Xi and Shun rather than Xizu and Shunzu.

proposals.before: In our dynasty, before Taizu's shrine Taizong was styled Filial Younger Brother, Zhenzong Filial Son, and the late emperor Filial Grandson.
proposals.after: In our dynasty, at Taizu's shrine Taizong was styled Filial Younger Brother, Zhenzong Filial Son, and the late emperor Filial Grandson.
proposals.reason: 太祖之室 is the Taizu chamber where the styles are used, not a sequence 'before' the shrine.

proposals.before: Bian and others rebutted: "From Tang to Zhou temple systems differed, yet all maintained seven generations.
proposals.after: Bian and others rebutted: "From the Tang to the Later Zhou, temple systems differed, yet all maintained seven generations.
proposals.reason: 自唐至周 in this Song temple debate is the span from Tang through the Five Dynasties Later Zhou, not a reversal back to classical Zhou.

proposals.before: Bian and others rebutted: "From Tang to Zhou, temple systems differed, yet all had seven generations.
proposals.after: Bian and others rebutted: "From the Tang to the Later Zhou, temple systems differed, yet all had seven generations.
proposals.reason: 自唐至周 here names Tang through Later Zhou, not ancient Zhou.

proposals.before: To destroy his temple and store the tablet in a flanking chamber, displacing the grandfather's honor and installing him below descendants, scarcely accords with filial intent toward ancestors or treating the dead as if living.
proposals.after: To destroy his temple and store the tablet in a flanking chamber, displacing the honor of the ancestral fathers and installing him below descendants, scarcely accords with filial intent toward ancestors or treating the dead as if living.
proposals.reason: 祖考 means ancestral fathers/forebears collectively, not a single grandfather.

proposals.before: Acting head Zhou Mengyang of the Court of Ritual argued: "Generations above Xizu are unknown, Xizu as founding ancestor is beyond doubt, and he should be paired with the Life-Giving Emperor."
proposals.after: Acting head Zhou Mengyang of the Court of Ritual and others argued: "Generations above Xizu are unknown, Xizu as founding ancestor is beyond doubt, and he should be paired with the Life-Giving Emperor."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 等 (‘and others’), which the Chinese and literal both record as co-speakers with Zhou Mengyang.

proposals.before: In 1078, the office for fixing border and temple ritual submitted a plan for eight temples in separate palaces, with the founding ancestor centered and zhao and mu divided left and right.
proposals.after: In 1078, the office for fixing suburban-altar and temple ritual submitted a plan for eight temples in separate palaces, with the founding ancestor centered and zhao and mu divided left and right.
proposals.reason: 郊廟 is the suburban (jiao) sacrifice and ancestral temples, not a geographic ‘border’.

proposals.before: In the sixth month of 1083, Empresses Xiaohui, Xiaozhang, Shude, and Zhanghuai were elevated and enshrined; following Empresses Zhangxian Mingsu and Zhangyi, after the rites they proceeded through the ancestral temple, performing only the elevation-enshrinement honoring rite and sacrifice to the seven household spirits, provisionally suspending the mid-winter offering, ordered by consort succession.
proposals.after: In the sixth month of 1083, Empresses Xiaohui, Xiaozhang, Shude, and Zhanghuai were elevated and enshrined; following Empresses Zhangxian Mingsu and Zhangyi, after the rites they proceeded through the ancestral temple, performing only the elevation-enshrinement honoring rite and sacrifice to the seven household spirits, provisionally suspending the first-month-of-winter offering, ordered by consort succession.
proposals.reason: 孟冬 is the first month of winter, not mid-winter; the idiomatic rendering misstates the seasonal offering that was provisionally suspended.

proposals.before: When Tang's Wenzong took the throne, Suzong was moved and Emperor Jing counted as one generation—the precedent is not remote.
proposals.after: When Tang's Wenzong took the throne, Suzong was moved and Jingzong counted as one generation—the precedent is not remote.
proposals.reason: 敬宗 is the temple name Jingzong; rendering it as Emperor Jing obscures the Tang emperor intended.

decisions.reason: 文安府君 is the deceased-official honorific Lord Wen'an; 府君 is not a prefecture, as the following 中丞府君 and 驍衛府君 confirm.
高、曾四代 names the four ancestral generations headed by the great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather; 'and above' reverses the range away from the four generations actually requested.

decisions.after: Tang's Zhongzong and Ruizong both occupied zhao positions, while Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong shared zhao and mu as one generation.
decisions.reason: 敬、文、武 are Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong, not Gaozu; the proposed Jing/Wen/Wu remains too clipped beside the expanded Zhongzong and Ruizong in the same sentence.
The speaker is 宋湜, romanized Song Shi; Wo does not correspond to 湜.
The same 宋湜 is Song Shi in the literal field; Wo is a misreading of 湜.
溫嶠 is Wen Qiao (Qiáo); Jiao is the wrong reading of 嶠.
僖、順 abbreviate the Song temple names 僖祖 and 順祖 of the two spirits to be moved, not Xi and the sage-king Shun.
The literal likewise takes 僖、順 as Xi and Shun; in this temple-count context they are Xizu and Shunzu.
太祖之室 is the Taizu chamber at which the styles are used; locative 'before' can be read as a temporal sequence the Chinese does not state.
自唐至周, after an appeal to recent practice, runs Tang through Later Zhou; the next unit's 自周以上 then turns to classical Zhou, so unglossed 'Zhou' here misleads.
The literal 自唐至周 is the same Tang-to-Later-Zhou span, not a backward leap to ancient Zhou.
祖考 is the collective honor of ancestral fathers, not a single grandfather.

decisions.reason: 周孟陽等 marks Zhou Mengyang and others as joint speakers; dropping 等 falsely attributes the memorial to him alone.
郊廟 is the suburban (jiao) sacrifice together with the ancestral temples, not a geographic border.
孟冬 is the first month of winter; mid-winter would be 仲冬, so the suspended offering is misdated.
敬宗 is the temple name Jingzong; 'Emperor Jing' truncates that title and blurs which Tang emperor is meant.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Gaozu was produced by misreading 敬; the source abbreviates Jingzong as 敬.
English Song Wo does not match 宋湜; the name is Song Shi.
The office-plus-name string likewise used Song Wo for 宋湜.
English Wen Jiao misreads 嶠; the name is Wen Qiao.
The extracted title Emperor Jing truncates temple name 敬宗; the supported English title is Emperor Jingzong.
